title: AGrail: A Lifelong Agent Guardrail with Effective and Adaptive Safety Detection
pdf_path: papers/AGrail_A Lifelong Agent Guardrail with Effective and Adaptive Safety Detection.pdf
threat_model_summary: A runtime guardrail inspects each proposed agent action against safety checks generated from guard requests; unsafe actions are blocked. The guardrail is an LLM system and can itself be wrong or attacked; no cryptographic adversary model.
core_contributions: AGrail: analyzer/executor dual-LLM lifelong guardrail with memory and test-time adaptation
Safety-check generation/merging and auxiliary tool-based checking
Safe-OS benchmark (100 cases) plus four existing agent safety benchmarks
Reports ~96.3% task-specific risk detection and 95.6% normal-action retention
limitations: Empirical LLM guardrail with no formal guarantee
Adaptive attacker and guardrail compromise not fully evaluated
theoretical_crypto_links: None; guardrail reasoning is not a cryptographic reference monitor
Formal noninterference/policy enforcement is our inference
applied_crypto_links: No encryption, signatures, credentials or TEE
Signed policy/action receipts are our inference only

title: Security Challenges in AI Agent Deployment: Insights from a Large Scale Public Competition
pdf_path: papers/Security Challenges in AI Agent Deployment_Insights from a Large Scale Public Competition.pdf
threat_model_summary: Large public red-teaming competition against 22 frontier LLMs in 44 simulated deployment scenarios; attackers use prompts and indirect injection. Measures policy-compliance failures, not cryptographic compromise.
core_contributions: ~1.8M attacks from ~2,000 participants across 44 scenarios
Session-level ASR 12.7%; indirect injection 27.1% vs direct 5.7%
Behavior-level and transfer ASR defined separately
Shows capability is only weakly correlated with robustness
limitations: Behavior-level '100% ASR' is an existence statement, not per-attack success
No confidence intervals or significance tests
Scenario coverage and judge policy limit validity
theoretical_crypto_links: None; competition and policy compliance are not cryptographic evaluation
Signed tool output/action receipts are our inference
applied_crypto_links: Only relevance is that authenticated provenance does not establish instruction legitimacy

title: WASP: Benchmarking Web Agent Security Against Prompt Injection Attacks
pdf_path: papers/WASP_Benchmarking Web Agent Security Against Prompt Injection Attacks.pdf
threat_model_summary: Attacker is an ordinary malicious user of a website (GitLab/Reddit) who can post issues/comments but cannot alter layout or others' content; the agent is black-box. 21 multi-step attacker goals and 37 utility tasks.
core_contributions: WASP benchmark on VisualWebArena GitLab/Reddit
Intermediate vs end-to-end ASR separation
84 attack tasks across two injection templates
Finds 'security by incompetence': high hijack rate but low end-to-end goal completion
limitations: Small task set (1 task = 1.19 percentage points)
theoretical_crypto_links: None; benchmark and prompt defenses only
Authenticated content provenance does not prevent semantic hijacking (our inference)
applied_crypto_links: Useful as evaluation harness for action-level authorization/capability mechanisms (our inference)

title: DRIFT: Dynamic Rule-Based Defense with Injection Isolation for Securing LLM Agents
pdf_path: papers/DRIFT_Dynamic Rule-Based Defense with Injection Isolation for Securing LLM Agents.pdf
threat_model_summary: Indirect prompt injection in tool results; DRIFT constrains plans, validates Read/Write/Execute actions against user intent, and isolates conflicting instructions before they enter memory. The validator is an LLM and not a cryptographic monitor.
core_contributions: Secure Planner with function trajectory and JSON parameter checklist
Dynamic Validator for Read/Write/Execute actions and user approval
Injection Isolator before memory writes
AgentDojo ASR 30.7% to 1.3% with modest utility loss
limitations: Injection isolation is string filtering, not cryptographic isolation
theoretical_crypto_links: None; no cryptographic definition or proof
Signed plans/capability tokens are our inference
applied_crypto_links: No encryption, signatures, MACs or TEE
Read/Write/Execute capability scoping could be cryptographically enforced, but not implemented

title: MCP-SafetyBench: A Benchmark for Safety Evaluation of Large Language Models with Real-World MCP Servers
pdf_path: papers/MCP-SafetyBench_A Benchmark for Safety Evaluation of Large Language Models with Real-World MCP Servers.pdf
threat_model_summary: Malicious or compromised MCP servers, hosts and users inject attacks across 20 types; 13 LLMs are evaluated on 245 cases. Measures behavioral attack success, not cryptographic compromise.
core_contributions: MCP-SafetyBench with 245 cases and 20 attack types across five domains
Taxonomy of server/host/user attack sources
Safety prompts largely ineffective; host-side attacks strongest
limitations: Behavioral ASR benchmark, no protocol-level instrumentation
Attack realism and case coverage limited
theoretical_crypto_links: None; MCP safety is empirical model behavior, not authentication
Signed tool manifests/version pinning are mentioned only as missing controls (our inference)
applied_crypto_links: No encryption, signatures, MAC or credentials implemented
Signed/versioned tool manifests and scoped capability tokens are natural but untested interfaces
